collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A young woman asks to train as a canoe builder: train her, or ask her to prove herself first.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has asked (friend), the master canoe builder, to take her as an apprentice. Some of the village has laughed: canoe building has always been done by men in (friend)'s family. (friend) has seen (subject) carve, and she is good. What should (friend) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) takes her on. The first year is hard: splinters, mistakes, and a lot of people watching for her to fail. She does not. Her first canoe is fast and true, and the people who laughed come and ask her to build theirs.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks her to build a small canoe on her own first. She builds it in a month, and it floats, and leaks, and floats again. (friend) takes her on. She says she would have preferred to be trusted from the start. (friend) admits she is right.
